Approval of a rezoning from various zoning categories to M- 1 ( Light Industrial District) Chair Williams opened the public hearing. Deputy Director Aron Hall came forward and presented a rezoning request (Z2024-003) to rezone railroad property and right-of-way from what it is currently zoned (which varies throughout the city) to a uniformed zoning of M- 1 ( Light Industrial District). The subject property totals roughly 6 miles in length and is developed by Norfolk Southern as an active rail line. The subject property bisects the City boundary line at Suwanee Creek on the northeastern entryway and runs through the City at its terminus running under North Berkely Lake Road to the southwest. The current zoning of the railroad right- of-way has been interpreted to begin at the center line of the track and run generally parallel to the zoning boundary adjacent to it. However, the railroad is not considered by all to be just right- of-way, but real property, and therefore must be properly zoned. 2 PC Minutes October 7, 2024 Page 3 of 7 Staff recommended that all railroad property and right- of-way be zoned M- 1 ( Light Industrial District) and be shown on the official zoning map of the City as such. There are a few spur tracks that exist within the City limits that do not belong to Norfolk Southern. These tracks are already zoned appropriately on the parcels that they exist on. Chair Williams called for questions/ comments from the public. Being none, Chair Williams called for discussion. Being none, Chair Williams called for motion. A motion was made by Commissioner Fisher, Seconded by Commissioner Baggett to approve case Z2024- 003. Voted for: Commissioners Williams, Moss, Gajjar, Baggett, and Fisher Motion carried.

Text Amendment to Article 9. Project Design and Construction Standards Section 915. 04 Easements Chair Williams opened the public hearing. Deputy Director Aron Hall came forward and presented Text Amendment (TA2024- 015). This past summer, the Stormwater Department employed two interns to survey drainage easements throughout the city and found an overabundance of trees within the easements. These drainage easements allow stormwater runoff to travel through underground pipes, or over shallow swales, and eventually to larger streams or rivers. 6 PC Minutes October 7, 2024 Page 7 of 7 For these drainage easements to function properly, they must be clear of large objects and debris. Furthermore, trees planted above stormwater pipes will eventually destroy the pipes as their roots grow and seek water. Staff is recommending that trees not be planted within a drainage easement and that only turf grass, ornamental grasses and/ or shrubs and/ or shrubbery not to exceed 2 feet at maturity be allowed to be planted within the drainage easement. Chair Williams called for questions/ comments from the public. Being none, Chair Williams called for discussion.
